author: Nick Ulivieri
text:
We've relied on City & Suburban Heating & Cooling for years when it came to HVAC repairs on old systems (old home and new) but the current AC/furnace we had was getting very close to the end of its life. After City & Suburban came out to repair our condenser unit this summer, we could have kept sinking money into repairs but we didn't want to be forced into an emergency replacement at an inopportune time in the near future. When Rob told us City & Suburban began doing full replacements earlier in 2025 (previously they only did repairs), we started researching replacement options...oh boy, did I learn a lot more about furnaces and A/Cs than I ever would have imagined. It was admittedly overwhelming.

We got a handful of quotes from a few firms - all of which had multiple different systems they tried to sell us on - but in the end we went with City & Suburban. Unlike the other companies we contacted, Rob (the owner) didn't hard sell us on the latest and greatest generation of HVAC systems with added bells and whistles. He laid out the few options best suited to our condo's layout, and importantly, was candid about the maintenance costs/challenges associated with top-of-the-line systems. To us, the word of someone who repairs these systems daily meant a lot more than someone who was only trying to sell them. Between our long-term relationship with City & Suburban, their very competitive pricing, and Rob's trustworthiness, it was a fairly easy call to make.

The day-of install was admittedly stressful thanks to the large investment, and morning thunderstorms attempting to foil our schedule. We had started this process a few months ago, and it was hard to part with our still-working, but very old, HVAC system we knew well...even with it's faults. Due to our building's height, we needed a crane to lift the condenser unit to the roof. Despite my early anxiety and the uncooperative weather, the crane waited it out and Rob's team got the lift done once the weather cleared and from there the hardest part was over. Rob was there for a portion of the morning to make sure the lift went well and that his installers were set with everything they needed. Once the roof work was done, the rest was smooth sailing.
